headline: Week 4 · Sun Oct 4: KC @ Las Vegas Raiders — Tuesday desk
dek: Tuesday Sep 29 desk: Kansas City beat Miami Dolphins (KC 24–10) on the road at Hard Rock Stadium. Where the Chiefs stand now, and the plan for Las Vegas Raiders.
videoHook: Let's get into it — KC: the last game, where we stand, and Las Vegas Raiders.
theEdge: Model/market read: the model gives KC 70.0%; Vegas has it KC -4.5; Polymarket prices the Chiefs at 8.6% to win it all.

storyline.lede: Kansas City turns the page to Las Vegas Raiders. the model gives KC 70.0%; Vegas has it KC -4.5; Polymarket prices the Chiefs at 8.6% to win it all. Last game on the tape, the current state of the roster, then the game plan and matchup for who's next.
body: This edition runs the weekly desk in order: last game, current state, next opponent.

A win over Miami Dolphins is still a win — even in August — because it is evidence the script can hold when the other side punches back. The box: ESPN had KC at 334 total yards against 329 for the opponent; turnovers KC 1 / opp 2; KC third downs 3-7. The tape to keep is how they scored, not that they did.
The 2026 Chiefs are 3-0 after the last kickoff. Coming off W KC 24–10 vs. Miami Dolphins. The next assignment is Las Vegas Raiders.

The matchup is a style question first: can Kansas City stay on schedule against what Las Vegas Raiders does best, and can Steve Spagnuolo make Las Vegas Raiders play left-handed? The market: the model gives KC 70.0%; Vegas has it KC -4.5; Polymarket prices the Chiefs at 8.6% to win it all. Give them credit in the trenches and on early downs; mark KC edges only where the personnel actually says so.

In tight games the margins live here.
Halftime adjustments are a Chiefs advantage.

xsandos.title: Inside zone — stay on schedule
xsandos.why: Early-down efficiency keeps the play-action and boot menu honest and the offense out of obvious passing downs — where opponents want it.
xsandos.coaching: One cut, downhill — let the double-teams move the line and take the four yards every time.

xsandos.title: Under-center boot — the early-down answer
xsandos.situation: 1st & 10 off a run look vs. Las Vegas Raiders
xsandos.why: Moves the launch point away from the rush and gives a defined half-field read — the cheapest explosive in the menu once the run game has landed.
xsandos.coaching: The fake has to match the run action on tape or the backside end never bites.

xsandos.title: 4 verticals vs. Cover 3
xsandos.why: Stretches the deep zones and forces the safety to choose — a staple answer when the defense sits back.
xsandos.coaching: Bend the seams to the hash and read the safety's leverage.

xsandos.title: Mesh vs. man
xsandos.why: Rub-heavy crossers beat man coverage and give a clean, quick answer with an RB checkdown as the outlet.
xsandos.coaching: Set the mesh depth tight so the pick is legal and natural.

xsandos.title: Simulated pressure on the money down
xsandos.why: Five-man picture, four-man rush: force the hot throw into a capped window without selling out the coverage behind it.
xsandos.coaching: The dropper must land in the throwing lane the protection leaves open — that's where the hot ball goes.

xsandos.title: Spagnuolo Cover-2 shell
xsandos.situation: Protect a lead / obvious passing down
xsandos.why: Takes the top off, rallies to tackle, and dares the offense to be patient — the situational change-up.
xsandos.coaching: Sink the corners, funnel everything to the deep halves.

coaching.detail: Win early downs, stay on schedule, and let the play-action menu do the heavy lifting.
Spagnuolo's disguise against the opponent's answers is the chess match to watch.
